summary: Eviatar Shulman works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1998–2008), where he later held posts in 2009 and as a Mandel postdoctoral fellow at the Scholion center (attested 2015).

Eyal Aviv is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1925–1934), where he succeeded Jean Philippe Vogel in 1939 and held a post until 1972.
Fa Qing specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Calgary, where his doctoral supervisor was Leslie S. Kawamura, with interim supervision by A. W. Barber.

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD from the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (~1992–1999) and became a Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

Fabio Rambelli works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell, and held posts at Sapporo University as Associate Professor (2001–2002) and Professor of Religion and Semiotics (~2000–2010).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004). She has held posts at the University of Florence (~2000) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".
Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-kuei Li specialized in linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology. After studying at Tsinghua University (~1921–1924) and the University of Michigan (~1924–1926), he held posts at Chicago (~1928–1929), Yale (~1937–1939), the University of Washington (~1949–1969), and Hawaii (~1969–1974).
Fausto Gherardo Fumi was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore's Classe di Lettere e Filosofia under Giuseppe Bardelli from approximately 1858 to 1862.

Fazun specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Wuchang Buddhist Institute, Tibetan School, and Drepung Monastery, and under Taixu. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and served at the Buddhist Academy of China as president (1956) and director (1980).

Ferdinand Benary was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied under Franz Bopp (~1824–1827) and became an associate professor in the theological faculty at the Humboldt University of Berlin in 1831.

Ferdinand Diederich Lessing was a scholar of sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a teacher at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1925–1935) and at the University of California, Berkeley (~1935–1952).

Ferdinand Justi specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1854–1856) and under Theodor Benfey (~1856–1859), later serving on the faculty at the University of Marburg (~1865–1907).

Ferdinand Sommer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1894–1896). He held posts at Leipzig, Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1926–1942).

Ferdinand de Saussure was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Geneva, Berlin, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius and Karl Brugmann. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1880–1891) and the University of Geneva (1891–1913).
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nalanda University under doctoral supervisor Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the National University of San Marcos. He held posts at the University of Buenos Aires (~1964–1984) and served as director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2017).
Filippo Marsili works in sinology and history/archaeology. He was a graduate student at the University of California, Berkeley, and holds a post at Saint Louis University.

Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. After completing his doctorate at Harvard University by 2015, he held a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale (2017–2018) and a post at Brown University (attested 2020).
